Before discussing our financial performance for the quarter, I would like to briefly introduce 
our business, our operating model, and the long-term opportunity we see ahead. Steamhouse 
pioneered the community boiler system in India. We sell steam and nitrogen to industries like 
chemical, pharmaceuticals, textiles, plywood, food processing, tyre industries, etcetera. 
 
These industries need steam for their heating and processing requirements, and have their own 
boilers for generating steam for their requirement. These industries have had to invest in their

own captive boilers, along with the associated land, fuel handling system, water treatment 
facilities, pollution control equipment, manpower, and maintenance, and all of these were 
mostly inefficient.  
 
By outsourcing their steam requirements to Steamhouse, these industries can now focus on their 
core manufacturing activities, operations, while we provide a reliable, efficient, and scalable 
steam solution. 
 
We believe our steam-as-a-service model represents a structural shift from traditional captive 
boiler ownership to outsourced steam solutions. By aggregating demand through centralized 
facilities, we provide customers with greater efficiency, reliability, and cost optimization, while 
creating a scalable business model for Steamhouse. 
 
Today, our business operates through three verticals: 
• 
Generation and distribution of steam,  
• 
Purchase and distribution of steam, 
• 
Generation Separation and distribution of Nitrogen. 
                                                Our business model creates value through scale. By serving multiple customers from a 
centralized facility, we operate larger and more efficient boilers, optimize fuel consumption, 
improve capital and capacity utilization, and spread infrastructure cost across a wider customer 
base. 
 
As highlighted in our investor presentation, community boilers can achieve thermal efficiency 
of 80% to 83% compared with around 50 to 65% for the conventional captive boilers. Our USP 
is our knowledge of steam distribution for kilometers. We have established more than 60 
kilometers of steam pipeline infrastructure across industrial clusters in Gujarat, enabling us to 
deliver steam directly to the customers with minimal pressure loss, while monitoring 
consumption in real-time. 
 
Our customer relationships are longstanding and sticky. Approximately 90.7% of our FY26 
revenue came from repeat customers, and we currently serve 21 customers with multiple 
operating units connected to our network. 
 
Most of our customers are covered by steam supply agreements comprising fixed and variable 
components, with the variable component linked to the coal price. This contractual structure 
enables us to pass through changes in fuel cost. In addition, newer contracts increasingly 
incorporate minimum guaranteed off-take commitments, providing better revenue visibility and 
facilitating the capacity planning. 
 
When evaluating new projects, we focus on customer tie-ups, contracted demand, and 
achievable utilization levels. As utilization improves, incremental steam volumes contribute 
meaningfully to the profitability because a significant portion of our infrastructure and operating 
costs are already in place. This creates operating leverage and supports margin expansion as the 
business scales.

Looking ahead, expansion remains one of our key priorities.We currently have four projects 
under execution at Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, and AMC (Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation) 
Pirana, along with three projects planned through IPO proceeds at Ankleshwar, Panoli, and 
Dahej. Beyond Gujarat, we are also expanding our footprint with a planned project at Tarapur. 
 
These initiatives expected to increase our steam distribution capacity from 345 tons per hour 
currently to approximately 705 tons per hour capacity, providing a strong foundation for long-
term growth. The long-term opportunity remains significant. Steam is a critical input across a 
wide range of industries, including pharmaceuticals, chemicals, textiles, food processing, paper, 
pulp, and tyres, supporting essential processes such as heating, drying, sterilization, and 
distillation. 
 
As industries continue to focus on operational efficiency and sustainability, we believe the 
centralized community boiler model remains significantly Underpenetrated, providing a 
substantial runway for the future growth. 
 
An important milestone in our expansion beyond Gujarat is our entry into Himachal Pradesh. 
We have been awarded the EPC mandate for setting up a 300 tons per hour community boiler 
facility at the Bulk Drug Park, Una, with a project value of approximately INR311 crores 
inclusive of GST. The project will also include long-term operations and maintenance. 
 
Importantly, the project is structured as an asset-light opportunity, with the project cost funded 
by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Limited. This allows us to bring our proven 
community boiler expertise to the new markets, while maintaining our focus on operational 
excellence and sustainable growth. 
 
Additionally, the Government of Gujarat's supportive policy framework, backed by capital 
subsidies for eligible projects, provides a strong tailwind for our long-term expansion plans and 
helps us expand our footprint across Gujarat.  
 
Alongside steam, we are also building a second growth vertical through industrial gases. We 
have commenced nitrogen generation and pipeline distribution at Ankleshwar , through a PSA-
based plant with a capacity of 350 Nm3 per hour, leveraging our existing industrial customer 
relationship and pipeline infrastructure. 
 
We intend to gradually scale this business by adding new nitrogen where commercially viable, 
expanding into industrial gases such as hydrogen and oxygen. This creates opportunities to 
deepen customer relationships, cross-sell additional products, and diversify our revenue streams 
over the long term. 
 
We are also actively diversifying our fuel mix by increasing the use of waste-to-energy solutions 
wherever commercially viable. Our experience at Vapi, along with projects under development, 
reflects our commitment to combining operational efficiency with sustainable energy solutions. 
 
Let me now briefly discuss our financial performance. Q1 FY27 was strong quarter for 
Steamhouse despite a challenging macroeconomic environment, marked by geopolitical

As we look ahead, our priorities remain clear. We will continue to expand capacity prudently, 
improve utilization across our network, execute projects on schedule, strengthen our presence 
in new geographies, scale our industrial gases business, and pursue sustainable energy solutions 
through greater adoption of waste-to-energy technologies.

operational excellence.  
•
